01 / THE IDEASIM RACING, EXPLAINED

Real racing skills.
From your own seat.

Sim racing means driving a virtual race car in a racing game or simulator. The car, track, grip, braking, and steering are represented on screen, and you control it with a controller, wheel, or other supported equipment. Some games are more accessible and arcade-like; others model car behaviour and race rules more closely, so “sim racing” covers a range.

The useful part is practising repeatable decisions: looking ahead, finding braking markers, guiding the car through a corner, and applying power smoothly. You can practise alone or race other people online, but you do not need a wheel, a special cockpit, or a subscription to begin learning the basics.

Those habits can help you understand racing, but a game is still a simulation: its physics and equipment differ from a real car. Start with what you have, choose one skill to work on, and build from there.
